title: Oilers sign Alex Formenton, acquitted Hockey Canada player, to 1-year contract
content:
The Edmonton Oilers have signed forward Alex Formenton to a one-year contract carrying an average annual value of $850,000, the team announced Wednesday morning.

Formenton is one of five former members of Canada’s World Junior team found not guilty of sexual assault charges in a July 2025 trial in connection with an alleged incident in June 2018, when a woman said she was sexually assaulted over several hours in a London, Ont., hotel room.

The NHL cleared the players to sign with NHL teams on Oct. 15, 2025. Goaltender Carter Hart signed with the Vegas Golden Knights shortly after, helping the team to the Stanley Cup Final.

In August, Hockey Canada announced continued suspensions for four of the five members, but reinstated Formenton effective immediately.

The 6-foot-2, 195-pound forward spent three seasons with HC Ambrì-Piotta in Switzerland, recording 33 goals and 19 assists for 52 points in 88 games. He did not play during the 2024-25 season after being granted a leave of absence, but rejoined the team for 2025-26.

Formenton made his NHL debut in 2017-18 with the Ottawa Senators and played 29 games over four seasons before skating in a career-high 79 games in 2021-22, recording 18 goals and 32 points. He also ranked second among Senators forwards with 150:27 spent on the penalty kill.

The Senators cut Formenton from their free-agent list in May, making him an unrestricted free agent.

Through 109 career NHL games, Formenton has registered 23 goals and 16 assists for 39 points while averaging 14:24 per game.

This story will be updated.
